name: 1736 Prairie Avenue — the Ingraham/McBirney house, its veranda front from the c. 1890 photograph, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D) at the 18th Street corner'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-2933 (piece 1 of T-1874) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id from the c. 1890 photograph of the house the Glessner House Museum reproduces (glessner_blog_1736_mcbirney_c1890_photo), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan. The draft's 5.5 m strip becomes the sheet's own main body, 23.3 m deep and 6.75 m along the street, on K01: two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard with two round-headed dormers on the street face, a bracketed cornice, three arched upper windows, and the photograph's timber veranda the front's whole width (the sheet's frame porch) on K07's terrace, with its stair at the north end. The camera is solved into data/reference_views/house_1736_prairie/mcbirney_c1890_photo.json; what the picture still shows differently is on its match record. T-2960 (piece 1 of T-2935) builds the upper windows' segmental heads under K09 cornice hoods on consoles, and the veranda's deck open beneath on its posts carried to grade, in painted timber with its balustrade. The street wall and the set-back front left of the house are T-2961's; the south flank's two projections and side porch, the service wing, the coach house and the mansard's date are T-2962's. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1736-mcbirney-2933/README.md.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1736 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1736 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The main body's rear south corner: the draft's frame point u 0.00, v -0.75 (draft position note: the rear corner of the main body's rectangle, lot frame u 22.750, v -2.125 m from the middle of the rear lot line, through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed; rotation -0.618 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line). Moved by T-2933 from the corner of the draft's fitted strip to the corner of the sheet's own plan: the trace's south wall runs at draft v -0.71 to -0.85 from the rear to the front, so -0.75.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1736-b1 p3) in the draft's lot frame: the rear wall at u -0.05 to 0.10, the front at 23.27 to 23.36, the south wall at v -0.71 to -0.85 and the north at 5.88 to 6.26 (its jogs are the sheet's printed figures, not walls), so 23.3 m deep and 6.75 m along the street. The photograph's front reads 216 px across at 32 px/m through its camera, 6.75 m. The south wall's two small projections (u 3.8-5.6 and 9.9-12.2, about 0.9 m out) and its frame side porch (u 16.3-18.9) are not built here (T-2935); the veranda (the sheet's frame porch p1/p2, 1.8 m deep the front's width) is the entrance kit's.

stories.note: Two storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, the attic storey in the roof: the photograph shows two rows of windows on the front under one cornice and the mansard with its dormers above it. The 1911 sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey (T-2933).

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the building pink, its brick ('3B brick dwelling'); the photograph shows the walls light, so painted (wall_finish).

wall_finish.note: The walls PAINTED over their brick, the paint opaque (T-2933: K01's paint otherwise tints the brick's map, and no tint of the buff brick is as light as this): the photograph shows them nearly as light as its sky against the dark sash, hoods and cornice shadow. The tone is read, the colour is not (the print is monochrome): a pale stone colour is RECONSTRUCTED.

principal_floor_m.note: The veranda's deck at the principal floor, its front edge at y 452 px through the camera (data/reference_views/house_1736_prairie/mcbirney_c1890_photo.json), 1.85 m over grade at the deck's face; the raised basement's lights show under it.

storey_heights_m.note: The bracketed cornice's soffit at y 194 px on the front through the camera, 9.9 m over grade, less the 1.85 m floor: 8.05 m for two storeys. The split puts the second floor 0.55 m under the upper windows' sills (y 300 px, 6.6 m); the principal storey is the taller, as the photograph's long openings behind the veranda say.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K03 common brick panel 1620 wears; painted over by wall_finish.

street_front_trim.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the principal storey's heads are hidden under the veranda's frieze, so the K01 flat lintel; the side and rear walls' segmental brick heads, as 1620's.

street_front_round_heads.note: T-2960: the upper storey's three street windows read off the photograph at 32 px/m: each light's head a segmental arch rising about 7 px (0.22 m) from rounded springs to its crown over a 28 px (0.95 m) span, so 0.22 of the span, and over each a flat moulded cornice hood about 54 px (1.7 m) across, its underside about 2 px over the crown, with a drop under each end standing just outside the jambs about 11 px (0.35 m) deep: the ends that turn down. Built as K09's cornice hood on its two scrolled consoles over a segmental hole cut to that rise, the block 0.25 m past each jamb so that with its cornice's 0.115 m return the hood stands about 1.7 m across. The hood's profile and the consoles' carving are the kit's (the print is too small to read them); a print at higher resolution would set both.

wall_head.note: A bracketed cornice under the mansard: the photograph's dark band of brackets across the front at y 186-196 px. Its profile and bracket spacing are not read; K10's bracketed timber cornice, round all four walls.

roof_form.note: A mansard: the photograph shows a steep lower slope from the cornice to a curb with round-headed dormers in it on the street face; the register's 'bounded mansard/attic treatment'. Its date (whether it was the house's first roof) is T-2935's to argue.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the mansard's upper deck at 10 degrees, as 1620's; no picture sees over the curb.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: 0.6 m, 1620's; the photograph's cornice projects about so far at the front's corners.

stair_tread_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: 0.28 m treads; the photograph's steps are seen edge-on and not counted.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The veranda's deck depth, which the stair rises to: the 1911 sheet's frame porch (s20fp-1736-b1 p1, p2) stands 1.8 m in front of the front wall the house's whole width.

stoop_width_m.note: The stair at the north end of the veranda between its cheeks, x 500-545 px at the deck's front through the camera: about 1.2 m between the north posts.

entrance_bay.note: The door behind the stair at the north end: the photograph's dark doorway at x 490-530 px behind the veranda, over the third bay's line.

front_bays.note: Three bays across the 6.75 m front, south to north, read off the upper storey's three windows through the camera (centres x 357, 423 and 496 px at 32 px/m from the eye's v 4.03): 1.12, 3.20 and 5.47 m. The principal storey's two windows and the door stand on the same lines behind the veranda.

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: five windows a storey along the 23.3 m south wall on 18th Street, rear to front, clear of the sheet's two projections (u 3.8-5.6 and 9.9-12.2) and side porch (u 16.3-18.9), which T-2935 builds; no picture sees the wall.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two windows a storey across the 6.75 m rear wall; no picture sees it.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the north wall stands 0.4 m inside the lot line toward 1730 and is built blank; no picture sees it.

sash_by_storey.note: The UPPER storey's sash read off the photograph through the camera: sills at y 300 px (6.6 m over grade) and heads (the arches' crowns) at y 240 px (8.6 m), 28 px wide at 32 px/m. The principal storey's are long openings behind the veranda whose heads the frieze hides (RECONSTRUCTED at 2.9 m from a 0.45 m sill).

roof_covering.note: The mansard's lower faces SLATED: the photograph shows them dark and even between the dormers, as a slated mansard reads. The deck's tin is RECONSTRUCTED (1620's).

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two stacks on the north wall's line; the photograph's trees cover the roof's crest and no stack of the house is read.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K04 half-round copper gutters and round downpipes at the rear corners; the photograph shows no downpipe on the front.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K06 two-over-two sash and area lights 1620 wears; for the arched upper windows (T-2960) K06's one-over-one segmental sash, the photograph showing each light's two sashes with no bars to read.

entrance_kit.note: The photograph's veranda (T-2933), the 1911 sheet's frame porch (s20fp-1736-b1 p1/p2) 1.8 m deep across the whole front: a deck at the principal floor (the stoop's landing and K07's terraces either side of it, south to the front's corner and north to its end), a turned balustrade along its front, four slender posts (x 337, 412, 484 and 535 px at the deck's front through the camera, 34 px/m there: v 0.15, 2.85, 4.9 and 6.6 m), a beam and a deep frieze over them (its soffit y 335 px, 5.25 m over grade, and its fascia y 300 px, about 1 m deep with the roof edge), and a low hipped roof from the wall. The stair rises at the north end between the last two posts (stoop_v_m 5.65 for the 1.2 m flight), straight out toward the walk, as the photograph draws its cheeks. front_yard_m is the street grid's: the front stands 9.07 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line (the draft's street_u 32.374 less the 23.3 m body) and the walk begins 1 ft further out. T-2960: the deck stands open beneath, as the photograph shows it: each post runs on down past the deck to grade (the posts' lower lengths stand at the same x 337-535 px, a pier under each), and between them the raised basement's front reads dark; built as K07's veranda `open_under`, the deck's skirt 0.2 m deep (the deck's front edge, y 450-457 px, 7 px at 34 px/m) and the void behind it set 0.5 m back (RECONSTRUCTED: how far back the basement's front stands under the deck is not seen). The balustrade is painted timber with the walls, a top rail at y 425 px (0.8 m over the deck) and slender balusters at about 0.14 m (the print shows the infill as a light pierced band, too small to read its pattern; RECONSTRUCTED). The frieze is one beam and the posts are plain square sections. T-2961: the roof's slope. In the print the band over the posts is a lit strip about 5 px deep along its foot (y 331-336, 0.15 m at 34 px/m) under a darker, textured band (y 306-331) that runs up to the upper wall, whose sills show over it at y 300-304. The strip is the fascia and the band the roof itself: a slope rising away from the camera shows from the walk whenever it rises steeper than the eye's line to it, and T-2933's (0.35 m over the roof's 2 m) rose at about the line's own 0.17, so it was seen edge-on and the beam's 0.6 m face stood where the print draws roof. Built now as the print draws it: the beam 0.1 m deep under a 0.08 m roof edge, 5.25-5.43 m over grade (y 336-330 px through the camera), and the roof rising 1.0 m to the wall, its ridge there at 6.43 m (y 306 px at the wall's 28.25 m), under the upper sills at 6.6. The texture (shingles or standing seams) is not readable at this scale and is the roof's own covering; nor is what the darker mark in the band over three of the posts is (x 340, 412 and 485 px against the posts' 337, 412 and 484), and nothing is built for it. The pitch is read through the camera's distance, like every height here (RECONSTRUCTED within it: L-k01-1736-mcbirney-veranda-2933).

boundary.note: T-2961: the photograph's low pale wall along the street line, read through its camera (data/reference_views/house_1736_prairie/mcbirney_c1890_photo.json), where the Prairie Avenue street line stands 18.9 m from the eye at 47.4 px/m and grade on it at y 536 px (the walk's own edge reads at y 535-537, which checks the camera). Its top reads at y 501 px from x 212 to 440 (0.74 m) and at y 491 px from x 476 to 628 (0.95 m); the step lies behind the street tree at x 456-472, s 4.2-4.6 m on the line, built at 4.3. The taller run ends at x 628 px, s 7.79, which is where the 1904 parcel's north lot line (data/street_grid/1904.json prairie_1736) meets the street line in this frame: the photograph and the parcel agree there without being fitted to each other. The line is the street grid's: the front stands 9.07 m behind it, and the lot runs s -0.65 to 7.79 along it (the parcel's corners taken into the house's frame). The wall's material is the Glessner House Museum's 2015 photograph of the McBirney curbstone still in place on the lot line (Prairie library a16-ghm-blog-1736-mcbirney-curbstone-2015, read 2026-10-21 from the image store's copy, sha256 e00ecb6a…; link only, so forms only are read): squared limestone blocks with a chamfered top arris, stepping up at one block, as the c. 1890 wall steps up. The wall reads continuous across the stair's line in the print (x 490-540 and 562-600 px), so no opening is cut; whatever gave onto the walk is hidden behind the tree or the ice wagon, and nothing is built for it. Nothing turns the 18th Street corner: no picture shows a return. The pier is the stair's: at the foot of its south cheek, whose top rakes down to it, x 475-507 px, its top at y 462, 1.55 m over grade at the foot's distance (and 1.56 m were it on the street line, so the height does not rest on where it stands); its lower part is hidden behind the street wall. RECONSTRUCTED: the wall's thickness (0.35 m) and the chamfer (0.06 m), the pier's section (0.6 m under a 0.06 m cap; the print's 32 px include its cap's shadow), and that the stone is limestone in c. 1890 as in 2015 (L-k01-1736-mcbirney-veranda-2933).

mansard.note: The mansard read off the photograph through the camera: its curb at y 103 px, 12.7 m over grade, 2.7 m over the eave; its lower faces near upright and straight. Two round-headed dormers on the street face, their lights at x 383-398 and 478-493 px (v 2.12 and 5.18 m at the mansard's face), sills at y 178 px and round heads at y 120 px. The two on the south face over 18th Street are RECONSTRUCTED: no picture sees that face.
